invariant: The note view an executor exposes is inert, capped data: guest writes to it never reach the host, the next call, or the next script, and it grants no capability of its own.

scenario.hostInput: a note listing (directives in document order, each with name, form, attributes, plain text) plus this script's position in the note
scenario.guestCode: list the note's directives; mutate an entry, its attributes, and the view itself; list again; enumerate every name the view exposes

mustHold: listing entries expose only the documented fields, and the view only the documented names
a mutation the guest makes is not visible to a later call in the same run, nor to any later script
content over the documented caps is reported as truncated, never raised as an error and never delivered whole
no ambient capability becomes reachable through the view: it is data, not a handle
a listing string reaches the guest with control characters and unpaired surrogates already removed, so no single character can truncate the payload
